newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court to hear travel ban request on Papon.
newsitem.headline: French court to hear travel ban request on Papon.

text.p: A French prosecutor will next week seek a travel ban on former cabinet minister Maurice Papon, due to go on trial in October 6 on charges of wartime crimes against humanity, a lawyer for victims' families said on Saturday.

Lawyer and Nazi-hunter Arno Klarsfeld told reporters he had been informed by justice authorities the Bordeaux prosecutor would request Papon surrender his passport and advise authorities of his movements ahead of the trial opening.
Justice authorities were not immediately available for comment. The travel ban request is expected to be made at next Tuesday's pre-trial hearing.

Papon, now 86, is accused of ordering the deportation of 1,560 Jews to Nazi death camps in 1942-44 when he served as wartime secretary-general of the Bordeaux region under the collaborationist Vichy government.
He has denied guilt and insisted he used his position to help the Resistance fighting France's Nazi conquerors.
Papon's lawyer, Jean-Marc Varaut, said that the prosecutor's move showed that authorities had pre-judged the verdict and that his client would not get a fair trial.
Varaut said Papon had never sought to evade justice during the many years leading to the trial.

Klarsfeld said there was a risk Papon would seek to flee aboard now that his trial was imminent. He added that restricting Papon's movements was a minimal move when people charged with far less serious offences were held in pre-trial detention.

Papon enjoyed an illustrious post-war career until the 1981 discovery of wartime files documenting his arrests and deportation orders. He served as Paris police chief from 1958 to 1967 and French budget minister in the 1970s.
